what: Authored ground truth for the dependent-substream merge: eight channels that name themselves, encoded by Dolby's own Dolby Digital Plus 7.1 encoder, decoded back and asked which channel carries which tone
why: every earlier check of the channel map compared oadec against another decoder. Agreement shows that two implementations do the same thing; it cannot show that either places a channel where the stream says it belongs. A signal that identifies itself can

material.authored: twelve seconds, eight channels, one sine per channel at -20 dBFS: 400, 630, 1000, 55, 1600, 2500, 4000 and 6300 Hz, written as a 24-bit WAVE-extensible file
material.encoder: DEE 5.2.1 `pcm_to_ddp` with `encoder_mode` ddp71 at 1024 kbit/s, loudness measured and not corrected (ddp71 refuses correction, and measuring leaves the samples alone), surround attenuation off
material.stream: E-AC-3 bsid 16, an independent substream with acmod 7 + LFE and a dependent with acmod 5 and chanmap 0x1a00, 375 frames each, 0 CRC failures, 0 decode errors

result_the_channels_carry_what_was_autho.method: projection onto a windowed complex exponential, four seconds starting one second in, for all eight tones in all eight decoded channels
result_the_channels_carry_what_was_autho.every_channel: carries exactly one tone at -20,0 dBFS -- its authored level to the first decimal -- and every other tone is at least 108 dB below it
result_the_channels_carry_what_was_autho.and_ffmpeg: gives the identical assignment, channel for channel, from the same stream. Two independent decoders and the authored signal all agree

result_the_core_alone_is_a_matrix.why_it_matters: this is what defect 1 delivered silently: not merely two channels short, but surrounds that are a mix of three signals
result_the_core_alone_is_a_matrix.merged: the same two channels, after the dependent is merged, carry a single tone each at -20,0 with everything else more than 150 dB down, and the back pair arrives as two new channels. Clause E.2.8.2's replace-and-add, measured

a_thing_learned_about_the_encoder.observation: DEE reads an eight-channel WAV as L, R, C, LFE, Ls, Rs, Lrs, Rrs -- the side pair fifth and sixth, the back pair seventh and eighth. The WAVE channel mask orders them the other way round: mask 0x63F is L, R, C, LFE, BL, BR, SL, SR
a_thing_learned_about_the_encoder.control: the same audio encoded again with the channel mask set to zero places the tones identically, so the encoder is not reading the mask at all
a_thing_learned_about_the_encoder.why_it_is_recorded: it silently swaps the side and back pairs of anything encoded from a correctly-tagged WAVE file, and it was nearly read as a decoder fault here before the FFmpeg control was run

regression_test: crates/oadec-cli/tests/real.rs, `the_merged_channels_carry_the_tones_they_were_authored_with`: every channel within 1 dB of -20 and at least 60 dB above the loudest tone belonging to another channel. Swapping the side and back pairs in the expectation makes it fail by 197 dB
evidence_hierarchy: this moves the dependent-substream channel map from `two decoders agree` to `authored ground truth with a reference encoder`, which is the top row of the hierarchy this project uses
